 For the first time in 30 years, a Quentin Tarantino movie is coming out where his only involvement was as a writer. With two weeks to go until the Tarantino-penned The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth hits IMAX, the MPA rating for the movie has been revealed.

 Quentin Tarantino's Cliff Booth Movie Earns R-Rating
 The Motion Picture Association has officially rated The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth "R", with its reasoning being that the movie contains "some strong/disturbing violence, bloody images, pervasive language, sexual content, nudity, and drug use."
 The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is a standalone sequel spinoff to Tarantino's Once Upon a Time in Hollywood , with Brad Pitt reprising his role as Cliff Booth, the former stunt double of Rick Dalton. The movie is set eight years after Cliff Booth encountered the Manson family in Tarantino's parallel history, in 1977 Los Angeles, which "no longer needs a hippie-slaying stuntman the way it did," per the official synopsis.
 "But Hollywood will always have problems, problems that can only be solved by someone with Cliff’s unique (occasionally extralegal) abilities. When he’s not earning his keep bartending or as a projectionist, Cliff Booth is a fixer — solving situations for Hollywood’s great and, sometimes, not so good," the synopsis continues.
 "He’s curious when he gets a call from talent agent Karen Crosby (Elizabeth Debicki), on behalf of her client, TV megastar Charlie Peters (Scott Caan) — a man known for doing his own stunts. And he’s further entertained and intrigued when he meets other characters in Charlie’s world, from his knowing wife Toni (Carla Gugino) to pro football champion turned screen star Roderick ‘Hot Rod’ Harrison (Yahya Abdul-Mateen II). Then there are the Verdusco brothers (Matt Groove and JB Tadena), mysterious gangsters causing mayhem across the city. What was once a fairytale is now a crime story — a cocktail of violence, ambition, and desire that could only happen in L.A.," concludes the synopsis.
 Quentin Tarantino's Tenth Movie Is Still on the Way
 Carla Van Wagoner/Future Image/Cover Images 
 Despite being a sequel to a movie Tarantino directed, the filmmaker did not return to the director's chair for Cliff Booth , as he did not want the movie to be his tenth and final directorial effort. Tarantino only wrote the screenplay, marking the first time since 1996's From Dusk till Dawn that he received a writer credit for a movie he didn't also direct. David Fincher instead helmed the sequel for Netflix , reuniting him with Pitt for the third time, after 1999's Fight Club and 2008's The Curious Case of Benjamin Button .
 Since Tarantino plans to retire after his tenth directed movie, the filmmaker has struggled to find the right idea to justify being his final feature. He's already scrapped The Movie Critic and redeveloped The Popinjay Cavalier into a stage play. Last month, he revealed that he's "written a script that I really like," but won't focus on it until after he's done with The Popinjay Cavalier , which doesn't officially open until March 2027 at London's West End.
 The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth will get an exclusive two-week run on IMAX screens ( just not the ones owned by Cinemark and Regal ) starting Nov. 25. It will then debut on Netflix on Dec. 23.
